info.name: AI Gateway - oauth2 policy
info.description:
End-to-end test collection for the oauth2 dev policy - grant-type agnostic (client_credentials and password both implemented), with a Redis-backed token cache shared across gateway-runtime replicas.

Companion to gateway/dev-policies/upstream-oauth2-authentication/TESTING.md - read that doc for the full narrative; this collection is the same flows as importable requests.

Prerequisites before running any folder here:
1. Start both mocks (see TESTING.md Part A):
   cd gateway/dev-policies/upstream-oauth2-authentication/mocks/mock-oauth2-idp && GOWORK=off go run .
   cd gateway/dev-policies/upstream-oauth2-authentication/mocks/mock-ai-backend && GOWORK=off go run .
2. Build the gateway with the policy included (Part B): cd gateway && make build
3. Bring up gateway-controller + gateway-runtime (Part C) via gateway/docker-compose.yaml. Add --profile redis (and list the redis service) if you want folder 04's Redis verification to have something to check:
   docker compose --profile redis up -d gateway-controller gateway-runtime sample-backend redis

IMPORTANT: requests to {{gatewayBaseUrl}} use a self-signed certificate (this mirrors curl's -k flag in TESTING.md). In Postman, disable 'SSL certificate verification' under Settings > General, or these requests will fail with a TLS error unrelated to the policy itself.

Run folders in order: 00 (health) -> 01 (register the AI APIs) -> 02/03 (test flows) -> 04 (Redis token cache verification, optional) -> 05 (cleanup).

variable.description: gateway-controller REST management API (LlmProvider CRUD), base path /api/management/v1
gateway-controller admin/health API (port 9094 when using gateway/docker-compose.yaml)
gateway-runtime (Envoy) data-plane traffic - self-signed cert, see collection description
mock-oauth2-idp (run natively on host via go run)
mock-ai-backend (run natively on host via go run)

request.description: Expect 200 'ok'.
Expect 200 'ok'.

Any response (even 404/401) proves Envoy is up and terminating TLS. Requires SSL verification disabled in Postman settings - see collection description.

item.name: 01 - Register AI APIs (LLM Providers)
item.description: Registers all six LlmProviders used by the test flows below, each using the typed upstream.auth.type: oauth2 field (no generic policies list needed).

request.description: Happy-path provider for E.1 and E.2 (caching).

body.raw:
apiVersion: gateway.api-platform.wso2.com/v1
kind: LlmProvider
metadata:
  name: oauth2-test-basic
spec:
  displayName: OAuth2 Test
  version: v1.0
  template: openai
  context: /oauth2-test-basic/latest
  upstream:
    url: http://host.docker.internal:9602
    auth:
      type: oauth2
      oauth2TokenEndpoint: http://host.docker.internal:9601/oauth2/token
      oauth2ClientId: test-client
      oauth2ClientSecret: test-secret
  accessControl:
    mode: deny_all
    exceptions:
      - path: /chat/completions
        methods: [POST]

request.description: Byte-identical oauth2 config to oauth2-test-basic (same clientId/tokenEndpoint/clientSecret/clientAuthMethod) but a completely separate API. item.name: 01b - Register AI Proxies (LLM Proxies)
item.description: Registered after 01 (LLM Providers) - oauth2-test-proxy references oauth2-test-proxy-backend by id, and the controller resolves that reference at proxy-registration time, so the backend provider must already be persisted first.

request.description: LlmProxy with oauth2 auth on provider.auth (LLMUpstreamAuth) - proves the oauth2 policy attaches and works through the LlmProxy path, not just LlmProvider.upstream.auth.

body.raw:
apiVersion: gateway.api-platform.wso2.com/v1
kind: LlmProxy
metadata:
  name: oauth2-test-proxy
spec:
  displayName: OAuth2 Test Proxy
  version: v1.0
  context: /oauth2-test-proxy/latest
  provider:
    id: oauth2-test-proxy-backend
    auth:
      type: oauth2
      oauth2TokenEndpoint: http://host.docker.internal:9601/oauth2/token
      oauth2ClientId: test-client
      oauth2ClientSecret: test-secret
      oauth2Params:
        testId: llmproxy-e2e

request.description: LlmProxy with NO provider.auth of its own, referencing oauth2-test-proxy-backend-ownauth (which has its own upstream.auth oauth2) - proves the provider's own auth still fires correctly when reached via the proxy's loopback hop, not just when the provider is called directly.

body.raw:
apiVersion: gateway.api-platform.wso2.com/v1
kind: LlmProxy
metadata:

request.description: LlmProxy with its OWN provider.auth (scope=proxy-hop-auth), referencing oauth2-test-proxy-backend-ownauth which ALSO has its own upstream.auth (scope=provider-own-auth) - both hops must independently fetch/cache a token (2 IdP calls), and the provider's own token (not the proxy's) must be what actually reaches the real backend, since the provider's hop runs last and overwrites the Authorization header.

body.raw:
apiVersion: gateway.api-platform.wso2.com/v1
kind: LlmProxy
metadata:
  name: oauth2-test-proxy-bothauth
spec:
  displayName: OAuth2 Test Proxy (both hops authenticate independently)
  version: v1.0

      oauth2TokenEndpoint: http://host.docker.internal:9601/oauth2/token
      oauth2ClientId: test-client
      oauth2ClientSecret: test-secret
      oauth2Params:
        scope: proxy-hop-auth

item.name: 04 - Redis Token Cache Verification
item.description:
Requires the stack to have been started with the redis profile:
  docker compose --profile redis up -d gateway-controller gateway-runtime sample-backend redis

Postman has no native Redis client, so this folder's real request just populates the cache (same call as E.1) - run the redis-cli commands below yourself afterward, from a terminal, to see the cached token directly:

  # List cached-token keys (upstream-oauth2:token:v1:<apiId>:<routeName>:<grantType>)
  docker exec gateway-redis-1 redis-cli KEYS 'upstream-oauth2:token:v1:*'

  # Fetch the cached token JSON for a key from the list above
  docker exec gateway-redis-1 redis-cli GET '<key>'
  # -> {"access_token":"...","token_type":"Bearer","expiry":"..."}

  # Confirm the TTL is positive and tracks the token's real remaining lifetime
  docker exec gateway-redis-1 redis-cli TTL '<key>'

To see the fail-open fallback (Redis down doesn't break auth):
  docker compose stop redis
  # re-run 'Populate cache' below - still 200 OK, just no longer cached anywhere
  docker compose start redis
